cosy-lesson.title: My Life With & Without Obsolete Jobs

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Anachronistic – belonging or appropriate to a period other than that in which it exists, especially old-fashioned.

p.em: Example: In our digital age, manual switchboards seem completely anachronistic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ubiquity – the state or capacity of being very common or omnipresent.

p.em: Example: The sudden ubiquity of smartphones has permanently altered face-to-face communications.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mechanization – the process of introducing machines or automatic devices into an activity or sector.

p.em: Example: Industrial mechanization historically forced manual laborers to find new ways of earning a living.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sentimentality – excessive tenderness, sadness, or nostalgic affection.

p.em: Example: We must separate pure sentimentality for old crafts from the practical realities of progress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Marginalize – treat a person or group as insignificant, peripheral, or powerless.

p.em: Example: Technological advances often marginalize older generations who struggle to adapt to new interfaces.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tactile connection – a physical, tangible link or interaction.

p.em: Example: Working with raw timber gave log drivers a strong tactile connection to nature.

cosy-blockquote.p: Streamlining – the design or organization of something to make it more efficient and simple.

p.em: Example: The streamlining of customer services has unfortunately resulted in the loss of human operators.

cosy-blockquote.p: Superfluity – an unnecessarily or excessively large amount or number; redundancy.

p.em: Example: The introduction of automated checkouts rendered human cashiers a sad superfluity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Omnipresent – widely or constantly encountered; widespread.

p.em: Example: The omnipresent screens of our modern world have completely altered our attention spans.

cosy-blockquote.p: Aesthetic charm – the visual or artistic beauty and appeal of something.

p.em: Example: The physical switchboard has a certain aesthetic charm that a modern server room lacks.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Not only did the knocker-up wake workers on time, but they also offered a highly personalized morning cycle; are modern ubiquitous alarms fundamentally anachronistic in their coldness?
★ Have you ever felt a deep sense of vulnerability when realizing how dependent you are on digital alarms?

Not only did the mechanization of agriculture displace thousands of manual laborers, but it also permanently altered the demographic structure of metropolises; was this transformation necessary?
★ What is the most physically demanding, repetitive labor you have ever personally performed?

Not only does uncritical sentimentality for old crafts blind us to their harsh conditions, but it also creates a false narrative of the past; how can we appreciate defunct jobs objectively?
★ Is there an outdated craft or trade that you find deeply fascinating or artistically inspiring?

Not only do automated systems marginalize mature manual workers, but they also accelerate social alienation; should businesses preserve manual tasks as a matter of social health?
★ Have you ever had to watch someone you care about struggle to adapt to new workplace systems?

Not only did physical letters offer a rich tactile connection, but they also forced us to slow down our social communication; is instant messaging making dialogue too shallow?
★ Do you still find value in sending handwritten cards or letters on special occasions?

Not only is systematic corporate streamlining rendering human administrative cashiers a sad superfluity, but it is also making public spaces completely cold; can we reverse this?
★ Have you ever worked in an environment where speed and metrics were prioritized over quality of interactions?

Not only did old manual jobs protect absolute personal privacy, but they also prevented the rise of omnipresent screens; is a digit-free career still viable?
★ How do you find a sense of true solitude and privacy in an interconnected world?

Not only did modern news feeds completely eradicate the theatrical town crier, but they also replaced human projection with algorithms; is modern public communication superior?
★ Do you feel overwhelmed by the constant stream of sensationalist news notifications?

Not only did manual switchboard operators act as the historic predecessor to automated networks, but they also kept human communication warm; was their redundancy inevitable?
★ Have you ever had an intimate conversation with a stranger that changed your perspective?

Not only do coal-fires and oil-lamps have an unmatched aesthetic charm, but they also offer a highly comforting light; does the smart home feel sterile?
★ What is the most visually atmospheric room or place you have ever stayed in?

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If manual labor becomes completely anachronistic, what new speculative fields will humanity invent to satisfy our natural urge for tactile creation?
★ If your job was fully automated tomorrow, how would you define your personal value?

If industrial mechanization eliminates all physical factories, how will communities redesign towns to preserve labor-based social cohesion?
★ Do you engage in hobbies like baking, gardening, or woodwork to maintain a connection to material reality?

If physical driving is replaced by autonomous AI networks, what new hobbies will emerge to satisfy our retro sentimentality?
★ Do you find pleasure in physical control over machines, or do you prefer to hand over control?

Without physical trades to marginalize, how will automated societies organize training for creative and analytical pursuits?
★ How do you feel when you look at artwork or read text that you suspect was generated by artificial intelligence?

Without a strong tactile connection to our objects and tools, what mental illnesses will humanity face, and how will we adapt?
★ What is your primary offline method for destressing and grounded reflection?

If the systematic streamlining of human conversation treats dialogue as a mere superfluity, how will we preserve genuine emotional intimacy?
★ Have you ever had a relationship or friendship that suffered due to over-reliance on text messaging?

When screens are omnipresent, what low-tech physical retreats will people design to find absolute serenity?
★ Have you ever gone on a "digital detox" weekend, and what did you learn from it?

If translation algorithms completely eradicate the need for human linguists, what new cultural codes will societies develop to preserve nuance?
★ Do you believe a machine can ever fully understand and translate cultural idioms and jokes?

Since printing was the predecessor to screens, what physical archiving traditions will we revive to protect knowledge when servers collapse?
★ Do you find yourself reading deep, long-form articles, or scanning short summaries and headlines?

If AI optimizes all architecture, what raw, imperfect design trends will emerge to restore local aesthetic charm?
★ What is the most beautiful city you have visited, and does its charm come from its old architecture?

ul.li: Incorrect: We discussed about the anachronistic quality of the work. → Correct: We discussed the anachronistic quality of the work. ((Grammar choice: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb that directly takes an object, not followed by the preposition 'about'.))

Incorrect: I was extremely interested about the lector's history. → Correct: I was exceptionally interested in the lector's history. ((Preposition choice: The adjective 'interested' is paired with the preposition 'in'.))

Incorrect: This system brings more better efficiency to the firm. → Correct: This system brings far better / significantly higher efficiency to the firm. ((Double comparative error: Avoid using 'more' with comparative adjectives like 'better'.))
